texts.preamble: Sri.Thimmaraju.E vs The Commissioner on 18 July, 2016 In The Court Of The 42nd Addl. City Civil & Sessions Judge At Bangalore City (Cch.No.43). Present: Sri.BAILUR Shankar Rama, B.Sc., M.A., LL.B.(Spl), nd 42 Addl. City Civil And Sessions Judge, Bangalore. Dated this the 18th day of July 2016. O.S.No.9306/2014 Plaintiff:- Sri.Thimmaraju.E., Physically Handicapped Person, S/o.Errappa, Aged about 30 years, R/at No.57, Doddakalasandra, Kanakapura Main Road, Bangalore-560 062. (By - Sri.Prem Kumar, Adv.) v. Defendants:- 1. The Commissioner, Bruhat Bangalore Mahanagara Palike, N.R.Road, Bangalore. 2. The Assistant Executive Engineer, Vasanthapura, Subramanyapura Ward No.197, Bruhat Bangalore Mahanagara Palike, Bangalore. (D1 - Smt.V.Prathima, Adv. D2 - Exparte) 2 O.S.No.9306/2014 Date of institution of the suit : 01.12.2014 Nature of the suit : Permanent Injunction Sri.Thimmaraju.E vs The Commissioner on 18 July, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/153573389/ 1 Date of commencement of : 06.07.2015 Recording of the evidence Date on which the Judgment : 18.07.2016 was pronounced Total Duration : Years Months Days 01 07 17 (Bailur Shankar Rama) nd 42 Addl. City Civil & Sessions Judge, Bangalore . Judgment
texts.facts: This is a suit filed by the plaintiff against the defendants for the relief of permanent injunction and costs. 2. The brief facts as averred in the plaint are that:- The plaintiff is a physically handicapped person and running a small petty shop in the suit schedule property since past 20 years under the name and style of Sri.Maruthi Condiment Shop, situated at Konanakunte Cross, Near Bus Stop, Kanakapura Main Road, Bangalore, measuring 6 x 9 feet, morefully described in the suit schedule. He has availed loan for Petty Retailer of Snacks / Tea Shop from Syndicate Bank, Doddakalasandra Branch, Bangalore, for an amount of Rs.3,00,000/- through SC/ST Scheme and also obtained subsidy from the said loan. The plaintiff submits that he has been paying monthly EMI to the bank from the earning of the schedule shop business, except that he has no any other source of income. He has installed electricity to the shop premises and has been making payment of electricity bills to the concerned authority. Thus, the plaintiff is in lawful possession and enjoyment of the suit schedule property. The plaintiff further submits that the officials of the defendants without issuing prior notice to the plaintiff, all of a sudden along with their servants abruptly came to the property on 02.05.2014 and tried to demolish the shop of the plaintiff. Somehow, he has thwarted their illegal acts. The plaintiff has applied for allotment of shop to run his business, but still the plaintiff has not received any letter with regard to his request. The defendants have flately refused for the same and threatened the plaintiff to dispossess him from the schedule premises. Again on 22.11.2014, officials of the defendants came near to the shop along with the JCB and police authority and held out repeated threats of dispossession and demolition of the schedule shop. The plaintiff lodged a complaint before the police. Left with no alternative the plaintiff filed the instant suit. Sri.Thimmaraju.E vs The Commissioner on 18 July, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/153573389/ 2 3. After the service of suit summons, defendant No.1 appeared before court through his advocate - Smt.V.Prathima and defendant No.2 remained exparte. The defendant No.1 - Commissioner, BBMP, filed the written statement, denying the allegations made by the plaintiff against the defendants. The said petty shop which the plaintiff has been erected on the footpath has not been covered by any permission from defendant No.1. The plaintiff claims that he is physically handicapped and said to have been running a petty shop on the footpath by raising of loan from Syndicate Bank under SC/ST Scheme and he has been making repayment of EMI, he has installed electricity to his petty shop and making payment of electricity bills to the authorities concerned, are all not within the knowledge of the defendant. The defendant No.1 submits that the plaintiff has not obtained prior permission of defendant No.1 for putting up petty shop on the foot path. The claim of the plaintiff that permission to run the business of condiments has been granted by the authority concerned is of no consequence to the case on hand. The defendant No.1 has directed the plaintiff to produce the copy permitting the erection of petty shop on the footpath, has failed to produce any such permission granted by defendant No.1. Hence, the petty shop erected by the plaintiff is illegal and is liable to be removed.
texts.arguments: Since the same is causing inconvenience to the pedestrians using the footpath. The defendant No.1 has intimated the plaintiff regarding the intentions of removing the petty shop, which is obstructing the free flow of the pedestrians using the footpath. The defendant No.1 contends that the plaintiff is of full knowledge regarding the drive taken by the defendant in view of directions issued by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka and the action taken by defendant No.1 is within the powers with defendant No.1 under Section 288(4) of KMC Act, 1976. The allegation that along with police men and JCB, the defendants came near the spot and held threat of dispossession and demolition of petty shop etc., are all false. The defendant No.1 is duty bound to revoke the encroachment made by the plaintiff on the footpath. The suit itself is not maintainable and liable to be dismissed for non- compliance of mandatory provisions of Section 482 of KMC Act, 1976. The plaintiff is guilty of suppressio veri and suggestio falsi and he has not approached the court with clean hands. The plaintiff has brought the suit with malafide intention to prevent the defendants from exercising or doing their lawful duty. There is no cause of action to file the suit and prayed that the suit be dismissed with costs. 11. The learned counsel for defendant No.1 has relied on a decision reported in 2009 (6) Kar.L.J. 453, in the case of V.Bramhananda v. Corporation of City of Mysore, Mysore and another, wherein it is held that if authority finds that temporary structure is causing inconvenience to public, it can refuse to renew license on its expiry and direct licensee to remove structure. In various decisions of our own Hon'ble High Court, wherein a specific direction was issued to the local authorities, not to permit petty shop to be erected on the footpath, which would cause hardship to the pedestrians in general. In the above said decision, it was held that the provisions of Karnataka Public Premises (Eviction of Unauthorised Occupants) Act, 1974, is not applicable to a temporary structure put up on the footpath. The learned counsel for defendant No.1 has relied on another decision reported in 1986 (2) Kar.L.J. 217, in the case Wajid.Y.S. & others v. State of Karnataka and others.
